name: Uri Geller
milestone_by_age_26: Became a well-known nightclub entertainer and performer across Israel by age 22-23 (1968-1970), performing in theatres, public halls, auditoriums, military bases, and universities with sold-out shows.
early_history_summary: Geller was born in Tel Aviv in 1946 to Austrian-Jewish and Hungarian-Jewish parents. After his parents divorced at age 10, he lived in Cyprus and then returned to Israel at 16, working in construction before joining the IDF Paratroopers Brigade at 18. He fought in the 1967 Six-Day War and was wounded. In 1968-69, he worked as a photographic model and began performing as a nightclub entertainer, quickly becoming well known throughout Israel.
family_context_summary: Geller was the son of Itzhaak Geller, a retired army sergeant major, and Margaret Freud. His parents divorced when he was 10, and his mother worked as a seamstress. He claims distant relation to Sigmund Freud on his mother's side.
parent_family_domain_summary: No clear evidence of family domain expertise in entertainment or performance. His father was a military sergeant major and his mother was a seamstress.
evidence_summary: Geller grew up in modest circumstances with divorced parents and served as a paratrooper in the Six-Day War before beginning his entertainment career at age 22. He leveraged his charisma and controversial persona to build a national following in Israel through nightclub performances and media attention. No evidence of family wealth, domain expertise, or institutional pipelines was found in reviewed sources. His early success appears self-created through street-level performance and controversy-driven publicity.

name: Mukesh Ambani
milestone_by_age_26: At age 24 (1981), Ambani was given charge of constructing the Patalganga polyester filament yarn plant, a Rs 100 crore project, after his father Dhirubhai called him back from Stanford MBA studies to join Reliance Industries.
early_history_summary: Born in 1957 in Aden (Yemen) to Dhirubhai Ambani, founder of Reliance Industries, Mukesh moved to India as an infant. He grew up in a modest two-bedroom apartment in Mumbai. He earned a BE in chemical engineering from the Institute of Chemical Technology, then enrolled for an MBA at Stanford but withdrew in 1980 at his father's urging to help build Reliance, which was then a small but fast-growing enterprise. At age 24, he was handed responsibility for the Patalganga petrochemical plant construction.
family_context_summary: Born to Dhirubhai Ambani, founder of Reliance Industries, and Kokilaben Ambani. The family lived modestly in a two-bedroom apartment in Mumbai until the 1970s, though the father was building what would become India's largest company. Mukesh never received an allowance and used public transportation.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father Dhirubhai Ambani was the founder and builder of Reliance Industries, directly transferring business acumen, industry networks, and a corporate platform. Mukesh was called back from Stanford specifically to work in his father's company.
evidence_summary: Mukesh Ambani's early career was defined by his father Dhirubhai Ambani's existing business platform. He was pulled from Stanford to lead a major industrial project at age 24, leveraging his chemical engineering training and his father's corporate infrastructure, licenses, and networks. The family lived modestly early on, but Dhirubhai was already building Reliance into a major enterprise. Mukesh's success at Patalganga demonstrated execution capability within an inherited business platform rather than independent creation.

name: Iman
milestone_by_age_26: Discovered by American photographer Peter Beard in 1975 (age 20) while studying at the University of Nairobi; her first modeling assignment was for Vogue in 1976 (age 21), launching a career that made her one of the world's most iconic supermodels.
early_history_summary: Born Zara Mohamed Abdulmajid in Mogadiscio, Somalia, Iman was the daughter of a diplomat (Somali ambassador to Saudi Arabia) and a gynecologist. She was sent to boarding school in Egypt at age four and later moved to Kenya with her family. While studying political science at the University of Nairobi in 1975, she was discovered by photographer Peter Beard, who paid her tuition equivalent for a photo session. Beard took the photos to New York, and Iman was soon brought over, landing her first Vogue assignment in 1976.
family_context_summary: Iman's father was a diplomat serving as Somalia's ambassador to Saudi Arabia, and her mother was a gynecologist. She was the first girl in her paternal family in six generations of sons. She lived with grandparents during formative years and attended boarding school in Egypt from age four.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in fashion or modeling. Her father was a diplomat and her mother a physician, providing an educated, upper-middle-class background but no direct fashion industry connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Peter Beard discovery,diplomat family,boarding school,physical distinctiveness,Vogue
evidence_summary: Iman's modeling career was launched by chance discovery by photographer Peter Beard at age 20, which gave her immediate access to elite fashion networks and a Vogue assignment within a year. Her family background was professional (diplomat father, physician mother) but not fashion-connected. Her distinctive Somali features and long neck made her an instant success in the fashion world. The mentorship and promotion by Beard served as the primary catalyst for her early career.

name: Maurice Gibb
milestone_by_age_26: As a member of the Bee Gees, Maurice Gibb achieved international chart success with 'New York Mining Disaster 1941' (April 1967, age 17) and UK #1 'Massachusetts' (September 1967, age 17), following earlier Australian success with 'Spicks and Specks' (1966, age 16).
early_history_summary: Born in Douglas, Isle of Man, Maurice Gibb began his music career at age 5 in 1955, joining the skiffle group the Rattlesnakes with his brothers Barry and Robin. The family moved to Australia in 1958, where the Bee Gees formed. By 1966, the group had an Australian #1 hit with 'Spicks and Specks.' They returned to England in early 1967, signed with Robert Stigwood, and quickly achieved international chart success with 'New York Mining Disaster 1941' and 'Massachusetts' that same year. Maurice served as bassist, guitarist, and vocalist for the group.
family_context_summary: Maurice was the son of Hugh Gibb, a drummer, and Barbara Gibb. He was born 35 minutes after his fraternal twin Robin, with older brother Barry. The family was deeply musical, with Hugh Gibb's drumming background and the brothers harmonizing from a young age. The family moved from the Isle of Man to Manchester, then to Australia in 1958 to support the boys' musical career.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father Hugh Gibb was a drummer, providing direct musical domain exposure. The parents actively supported and managed the brothers' musical development, relocating from the Isle of Man to Manchester and then to Australia to advance their career opportunities.
evidence_summary: Maurice Gibb's career was defined by the sibling collaboration with brothers Barry and Robin from age 5, creating one of the most successful pop groups in history. His father Hugh was a drummer, providing early musical exposure, and the family relocated internationally to support the boys' career. The brothers accumulated thousands of hours of performance and harmonizing practice before their international breakthrough at ages 16-17. The high-trust sibling team, combined with early performance experience and manager Robert Stigwood's network, created a uniquely powerful launch platform.

name: Akinori Nakayama
milestone_by_age_26: Won six medals including three gold at the 1966 World Championships in Dortmund (age 23), then became the most successful male athlete at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics with four gold, one silver, and one bronze (age 25).
early_history_summary: Born in Nagoya, Japan, Nakayama was a graduate of Chukyo University in Nagoya. He won the all-around at the 1965 and 1967 Universiade competitions. His first major international breakthrough came at the 1966 World Championships in Dortmund, where he won six medals including three gold (team, floor exercise, horizontal bar). He followed this with four gold medals at the 1968 Olympics, becoming the most successful male athlete of those Games.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Nakayama was born in Nagoya and graduated from Chukyo University, but family background details were not found.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chukyo University,Japanese gymnastics system,1965 Universiade,world champion,Olympic champion
evidence_summary: Nakayama was a product of the dominant Japanese men's gymnastics pipeline of the 1960s, graduating from Chukyo University in Nagoya, a city with strong gymnastics traditions. He won the Universiade all-around in 1965 (age 22) and 1967, demonstrating early competitive success before his World Championship breakthrough at 23. The Japanese gymnastics system provided elite coaching, training facilities, and a competitive team environment. Family background details were not documented in reviewed sources, so early-advantage scores are conservative.

name: István Sándorfi
milestone_by_age_26: Had his first individual exhibition at a small gallery in Paris at age 17 (1965), followed by a second exhibition in 1966, and his first significant museum exhibition at the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris in 1973 (age 25).
early_history_summary: Born in Budapest in 1948, Sándorfi's father was director of IBM in Hungary, which led to the father's imprisonment under the Communist regime and the family's deportation to a village. During the 1956 Hungarian uprising, the family fled to Germany and then France. Deeply affected by the violence of the revolution, István took refuge in drawing and then oil painting at age 12. Art became his overriding passion, and at age 17, while still in secondary school, he had his first solo exhibition in Paris. He later attended the École des Beaux-Arts and École des Arts Décoratifs.
family_context_summary: Sándorfi's father was director of IBM in Hungary, indicating an upper-middle-class professional background. The father was imprisoned for five years under Communist rule due to his IBM association, and the family was deported to an isolated village before fleeing Hungary in 1956. The family eventually settled in France.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in visual arts. His father was a corporate executive (IBM director), not an artist. However, the family's professional status may have facilitated access to education and galleries in Paris after emigration.
primary_early_advantage_tags: 1956 refugee,father imprisoned,self-taught painting,Paris galleries,obsessive practice,oil painting age 12
evidence_summary: Sándorfi's early career was shaped by the trauma of his father's imprisonment and the family's flight from Hungary in 1956. He channeled this into an obsessive dedication to drawing and painting from age 12, producing work mature enough for a solo gallery exhibition by age 17. His father's professional background (IBM director) provided some cultural capital but no direct art-world connections. The displacement to Paris placed him in a major art capital, and his self-driven, visceral approach to painting set him apart. His father later enrolled him at the École des Beaux-Arts to give him a more prestigious status.

name: Oliviero Toscani
milestone_by_age_26: After graduating from the Kunstgewerbeschule Zürich in 1965 (age 23), Toscani published his first fashion story in Annabelle magazine, leading to work with Harper's Bazaar and his first Vogue Italia shoot in 1967 (age 25), establishing him with major international fashion magazines by his mid-20s.
early_history_summary: Born in Milan in 1942, Toscani grew up in his father Fedele Toscani's photographic world. His father was a famous photojournalist for Corriere della Sera, and Toscani acted as his lab assistant and messenger from childhood. He had his first published photo at age 14. He studied photography and graphic design at the Kunstgewerbeschule Zürich from 1961 to 1965, learning from teachers who came directly from the Bauhaus. After graduating, his first reportage story of a girl in a miniskirt was published by Annabelle magazine, which led to fashion photography work for Harper's Bazaar, French Elle, and Italian and British Vogue.
family_context_summary: Toscani was born into a photography family. His father Fedele Toscani was a renowned photojournalist for Corriere della Sera, famous for photographing the hanging corpses of Mussolini. Toscani acted as his father's lab assistant and messenger from a young age, giving him early immersion in the world of photojournalism. He had his first published photo at age 14.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father Fedele Toscani was a prominent Italian photojournalist who founded the Publifoto and Rotofoto photographic agencies and worked for Corriere della Sera. This provided direct domain expertise, darkroom access, press contacts, and an early understanding of the power of images.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father photojournalist,darkroom access,Corriere della Sera,Kunstgewerbeschule Zurich,Bauhaus teachers,Vogue Italia,fashion photography
evidence_summary: Toscani's early career was built on a deep family-domain apprenticeship: his father was a famous photojournalist who provided darkroom access, press world exposure, and an early understanding of visual storytelling from childhood. This was complemented by formal training at the Kunstgewerbeschule Zürich under Bauhaus-trained teachers. By his early 20s, he was working for major international fashion magazines including Vogue Italia, Harper's Bazaar, and French Elle. His father's profession gave him both technical skills and industry fluency that most young photographers would lack.
